prompt_text: I want to sell my house in Pleasanton. Which specific real estate agents should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best real estate agent in Pleasanton CA to sell my house?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — but first I need one quick clarification: which Pleasanton do you mean (Pleasanton, CA or another Pleasanton)? And tell me any preferences (target price range, how fast you want to sell, do you want a top-dollar/luxury agent vs. a low-commission/flat-fee option).

If you want specific agent names now, I’ll need the city and a go-ahead to look up current top producers. Without live lookup, I can’t reliably list up-to-date individual agents, but I can tell you exactly which types of agents you should call and how to identify the best specific agents for your property. Below is a fast, practical plan you can use immediately.

Who to call (3–4 types)
- Top neighborhood listing agent(s): agents who have recently sold multiple homes in your exact neighborhood or subdivision. They get the best comps and buyer networks for your street.
- High-volume/team agent from a major local brokerage: good for wide exposure and fast buyer flow (Compass, Keller Williams Tri-Valley, Coldwell Banker, etc., in Pleasanton, CA).
- Boutique/marketing-focused agent: experienced with professional staging, photography, targeted digital marketing and social media — useful if you want top dollar.
- Discount or flat-fee listing service (optional): if commission is your main concern and you are comfortable handling some tasks yourself.

How to find specific names quickly
- Zillow/Redfin/Realtor.com: search recent sold listings in your address or neighborhood; note the listing agent names and call their offices.
- MLS solds (through an agent or some public tools): filter by neighborhood and date to see who’s closing deals.
- “Sold” signs and county recorder: drive the neighborhood and take down agent names/phone numbers on recent sold signs.
- Local Facebook groups/Nextdoor: ask neighbors who they recommend and for recent experiences.
- Brokerage local offices: call the Pleasanton branch of Compass, Keller Williams Tri-Valley, Coldwell Banker and ask which agents recently sold homes like yours.

What to ask when you call/interview (script + essential questions)
- Quick intro: “I’m considering selling my home at [address/neighborhood]. How many homes like mine have you listed and sold in the past 12 months?”
- Ask for a Comparative Market Analysis (CMA): “Can you prepare a CMA and recommend a listing price strategy? What price would you start at and why?”
- Marketing plan: “Describe your marketing plan (photos, floorplans, virtual tours, open houses, online ads, social media, staging). What’s included vs. extra cost?”
- Results metrics: “What is your average days on market, list-to-sale price ratio, and percentage of buyers you bring vs. other agents?”
- Fees and contract terms: “What’s your commission, any seller-paid closing costs you expect, and your listing agreement length/cancellation policy?”
- References: “Can you share 2–3 recent seller references in my neighborhood?”
- Negotiation: “Give one example of a negotiation where you got a seller more than list price or handled a tricky inspection.”

How to compare candidates
- Local track record: prioritize agents who recently sold comparable homes nearby.
- Marketing specifics: look for professional photography, floor plans, staging, targeted online ads, broker previews.
- Pricing strategy: beware of agents who always promise highest price without data — prefer clear CMA-backed plans.
- Communication style and availability: choose someone who responds quickly and lays out a clear timeline.
- Net sheet: ask each agent for a seller net sheet (projected proceeds) at several price points.

Red flags
- Vague or no CMA
- No recent comparable sales in your neighborhood
- Overpromising (guaranteed top price) with no data
- High-pressure to sign immediately without written plan

Call/email script you can copy
“Hi, I’m [name]. I own a home at [address/neighborhood] and am preparing to sell. I’d like a CMA and your written marketing plan. I’m interviewing several agents this week — could we meet for 30 minutes and can you bring examples of recent comparable sales and references?”

If you want, I can:
- Look up and provide a tailored shortlist of 3–5 specific agents in Pleasanton (I’ll need the exact city and permission to search current listings), or
- Draft an email or phone script tailored to your property (include address, home size, beds/baths, recent updates and your timeline).

Which would you prefer?
